questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me to choose a destination where english was the native language in order to improve my English. Other than that I wanted to experience a university which ranked higher than UCPH. However, the main reason that I prioritized USYD over for example Singapore were the opportunities to experience the unique nature in Australia during my exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was pretty easy to find information that I needed upon arrival. USYD sent out a lot of e-mails in the months preceding my arrival containing basically everything I needed to know for the first few weeks of being there. It was almost bordering on too much since it also covered basic stuff like remember to have your boarding passes printed for boarding the plane etc. 
There were also study abroad advisers from USYD that were available to answer any possible questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were several introductory "lectures" that could be attended even before the official orientation week started to learn about life in Sydney/Australia with information concerning shopping, banking, public transport use etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was very difficult to find housing off campus. Sydney is going through a rental crisis which means that renting is expensive and there are a lot of people looking for housing which makes it even more difficult to find an apartment for only 5 months. On top of that there are also a lot of scams that you have to watch out for. One website that I used to find my apartment was
realestate.com.au
since it only allows for real estate agents to post listings. Also be aware that due to the rental crisis it is now common to pay two weeks rent upfront if you are offered an apartment to show you are serious about your application/secure the apartment. When we first heard about it, we were sure it was a scam but we spoke with several real estate agents who assured us it was normal. We also ended up doing it when we were offered an apartment and everything was in order and the the first two weeks of rent were covered by our upfront payment.
I'd honestly recommend finding housing through USYD if possible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive, it takes a lot of time since you have to attend a lot of different open houses, it takes time away from exploring the city when you've just arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You receive a list of courses available for selection, you select the ones you want and after that you receive a list of which courses you were approved for/had space and then from that list you select four courses that you wish to attend.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a study abroad adviser that you can email with questions regarding the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was only one class that I didn't get even though I selected it as there weren't any more slots in the class. Apart from that I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to look at the exams. Some classes have 80 minute pen and paper exams which makes it difficult if you have terrible handwriting (like me).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was about the same as at UCPH, however, it is made more difficult as you (presumably) arrive without a common law background and no knowledge of the Australian legal system and how their federal and state legislation interact with each other.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was pretty similar to UCPH with a mix between lectures and classes wherein student participation was expected. However, there is more work spread out through the entire semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LAWS5143 Interpretation 
LAWS5151 Media Law: Contempt and Open Justice 
LAWS5180 IP: Copyright and Designs 
LAWS5183 War Law: Use of Force and Humanitarian Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend War Law. The subject matter is really interesting and the lecturer is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about the field. The context in which law is used is also very different from any other course I've ever had.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't really run into any unexpected costs, however, I did spend more money on travelling around Australia than I was expecting. Completely worth it though!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were actually more expensive than I expected. Coffee was less expensive (thankfully).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were a lot of activities available to students. At the beginning of the semester there is a big welcome fest in which all the clubs at the univeristy set up a booth to promote their club. These clubs basically cover every interest imaginable from bible study to anime to Taylor Swift to food. There are also two gyms on campus that it is possible to sign up for which includes access to a climbing center, swimming pool etc.
There are also a lot of political rallies on campus that it is possible to attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Personally I didn't join any of the clubs but I travelled as often as possible. I would definitely recommend travelling around Australia whenever possible. It is an amazing country!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
If it is just a day trip then going to the Blue Mountains two hours away from Sydney is amazing. There is a hike called the Grand Canyon walk which is beautiful. 
During the springbreak I did a roadtrip on the east coast which was amazing. I'd definitely recommend doing a roadtrip like that to see the Daintree Rainforest, the Great Barrier Reef, Magnetic Island and more. The sights and nature there is simply amazing. 

I'd also reommend visiting Tasmania if you get the time. The people down there are very welcoming and has some of the most beautiful hikes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Incredibly easy. I didn't really run into any problems.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't really run into any cultural differences that I found challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the openness of Australians. People very very nice and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find housing through USYD
2. Remember to look at what kind of exams the different classes have
3. Remember to enjoy your time. Time passes by quickly

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The workload is spread out over the entire semester instead of being focused on a few weeks of exams. Also be aware that certain clashes can occur with exams as you may have two short term exams on top of each other. I ended up with a three-day and a weeklong written exam that both had the same due date.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting fellow exchange students and the entire experience of living in a new country and city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
